rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah’s central theme explains the unique mention of Noah’s 950 years: truth’s advocates may face a long trial, as Noah did before fulfilling his charge and succeeding.
rows.anchor: It is actually the central theme of the sūrah which entailed this mention.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah’s stated age of 950 years agrees exactly with the Torah’s account of his life after the flood.
rows.anchor: The age of Noah (sws) mentioned here is exactly in accordance with the Torah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah gives Noah’s father and forefathers lifespans of 773 to 969 years; with no compiled history to contradict it, their longevity is plausible in early society and accords with divine wisdom and human nature.
rows.anchor: there is no reason to deny this information. It may also be kept in mind that in those times

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah’s people received respite only for a limit before God seized them; punishment was just because truth had been conclusively conveyed, while truth’s advocates are tested before success.
rows.anchor: the proponents of falsehood are conclusively communicated the truth before they are punished

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Noah’s long struggle, God saved him and his followers and made the event a sign in which advocates of truth and falsehood can see their respective fates.
rows.anchor: after such a long struggle and period of trial came the phase in which God delivered Noah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “made it” refers to the whole preceding incident, a common Arabic usage of pronouns.
rows.anchor: This is a very common usage of pronouns in Arabic.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can answer for another’s deeds: even Noah, a great prophet, could not save his son from God’s punishment.
rows.anchor: Had there been any possibility of this, Noah (sws) would certainly have saved his son from God’s punishment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As with Noah, Abraham was sent as a messenger to call his people to worship God and fear His wrath; the warning is timely counsel for them.
rows.anchor: just as God sent Noah (sws) to his nation as a messenger, similarly He also sent Abraham (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Fear God” means avoiding His wrath by not associating partners with Him in worship.
rows.anchor: means fear God ie. do not invite His wrath by associating partners with Him in worshipping Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worshipped deities are baseless idols and shrines; the claim that God made them His partners is fabricated, without divine statement or proof.
rows.anchor: The verse states that the deities which these people are worshipping are baseless. They are merely idols and shrines.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deities cannot provide sustenance; God alone controls it, so people must ask Him for provision.
rows.anchor: Everything is in the power of God alone. So if they need livelihood and sustenance, they must turn to God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone deserves gratitude as the giver of everything; associating partners with Him is ingratitude.
rows.anchor: by associating partners with the being Who grants everything, they should not show ingratitude to Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People will be raised and returned to God, and their idols will be useless to them.
rows.anchor: after denying, people will be raised up and meet God. On that day, their idols and deities will be of no use to them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s deniers are warned that earlier nations also denied messengers and met their fate; the messenger’s sole duty is clear communication, which Abraham fulfilled, leaving his people accountable.
rows.anchor: the only responsibility of the Messenger is to clearly communicate the words of God. Abraham (sws) has fulfilled this responsibility.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 19–23 interrupt Abraham’s invitation as a divine insertion: after he mentions the Hereafter, God supplies arguments for it suited to the circumstances of that time.
rows.anchor: Verses 19 to 23 are an insertion from God in between Abraham’s invitation to his nation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s bringing a dry, barren land to life shows that recreating people after they become dust is no difficulty for Him.
rows.anchor: when it is of no bother to God to transform a dry and desolate piece of land into lush green territory

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recreation should not seem improbable: the God who created everything from nothing and continually displays creative power can recreate humankind.
rows.anchor: people should not regard this to be an improbable happening. It is very easy for the God Who created everything from nothingness

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Travel and reflect on the world’s cycles of creation, destruction, and renewal—from nations and seasons to day and night—as evidence that resurrection is within God’s power.
rows.anchor: He brings a nation into being and then destroys it and brings a new one in its place. The day appears after the night and the spring after autumn.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universe itself supplies sufficient evidence for monotheism, the Hereafter, and reward and punishment; no external proof is needed.
rows.anchor: this world in itself is a complete workshop. There is no need to find any external proof of monotheism, hereafter and reward and punishment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding passage teaches that judgement of every matter ultimately belongs to God and reassures the Prophet not to fret over the arrogant, whose deeds’ consequences God will show.
rows.anchor: the judgement of all matters finally rests with God. At the end of this section, the Prophet (sws) is assured that he should not fret

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents’ own confession that God created heaven and earth entails that He alone deserves worship and gratitude; He is self-sufficient, sovereign, and needs no intercessor to win His favour.
rows.anchor: They confess that the heavens and the earth are created by God. So the question is that when He is the creator, how can someone else be worthy of worship and gratitude?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universe contains such abundant signs of God’s power and wisdom that even all trees as pens and all seas plus seven more as ink could not record them.
rows.anchor: if all the trees become pens and all the seas together with seven more become ink, it is still not possible to note down all these signs.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating every human is as easy as creating one soul; night and day obey God, He knows everything, and another authority in the universe would have ruined it.
rows.anchor: It is as easy for Him to create every human being as it is easy for Him to create a single soul. The night and day are subservient to Him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In hardship and ease, people should be patient and grateful; the favours they enjoy demand gratitude to God and remembrance of the Judgement Day.
rows.anchor: they should show patience in strife and gratitude in comfort. The favours they enjoy today entail that they show gratitude to God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coming Judgement cannot be denied because its timing is unknown: many realities have unknown arrival times, and true knowledge rests with God.
rows.anchor: The Day of Judgement is bound to come. It cannot be denied merely on the basis that its time of arrival is not known.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The isolated letters were discussed comprehensively in the commentary on Sūrah al-Baqarah.
rows.anchor: A comprehensive discussion on the isolated letters ( ḥurūf-i muqaṭṭa‘āt) was done in Sūrah al-Baqarah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative “these” refers to Alif Lām Mīm, which the author calls the Qur’ānic name of the sūrah.
rows.anchor: This is the Qur’ānic name of the sūrah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wise Book’s revelations are guidance and mercy for muḥsinūn, people who act fittingly, use their intellect well, preserve their natural traits, and act with insight.
rows.anchor: people who do everything in a befitting way and who have correctly used their powers of intellect and kept alive the traits of their nature

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If people disregard the Book, the fault is their perverted nature rather than a flaw in the Book; the Prophet should not be dejected by them.
rows.anchor: this is not because the Book itself has some flaw – rather it is these people whose nature is perverted. Hence, the Prophet (sws) should not become dejected

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding description of upright people is exemplified by those diligent in prayer, vigilant in zakāh, and convinced of the Hereafter; their conviction drives their diligence.
rows.anchor: it is these people who are diligent in their prayer and vigilant in giving zakāh and have conviction in the Hereafter.
